prompts.leak_audit_notes: This prompt tests a basic RSI mean-reversion strategy on SPY at daily resolution. Key LEAN-specific failure modes include: (1) incorrect RSI period — the prompt says '10-day RSI' so the model must use period=10, not the default 14; (2) forgetting to warm up the RSI indicator before trading begins, which can cause premature signals on the first few bars; (3) using self.RSI() shorthand vs. manual indicator registration with RegisterIndicator(); (4) not checking IsReady before acting on indicator values; (5) ambiguity around whether to hold a full position or partial — the prompt says 'buy' and 'sell' without specifying quantity, so the model must make a reasonable assumption (e.g., SetHoldings or a fixed share count). The exit condition (RSI > 70) only triggers if already long, which requires position-state awareness. Minor variation is expected around order sizing and whether to use MarketOrder vs. SetHoldings.
prompts.original_text: Buy SPY when 10-day RSI drops below 30, sell when RSI rises above 70. Daily resolution.
prompts.reformulated_text: Buy SPY when 10-day RSI drops below 30, sell when RSI rises above 70. Daily resolution.

prompts.leak_audit_notes: This prompt tests a classic RSI-based mean-reversion strategy on SPY at daily resolution. The core LEAN failure modes to watch for include: (1) incorrect RSI period — must be 14, not a default like 2 or 10; (2) failure to warm up the RSI indicator before trading begins, which can cause premature signals on the first few bars; (3) using self.RSI() shorthand vs. manually creating and registering the indicator — both are valid but warmup handling differs; (4) not checking indicator readiness (IsReady) before evaluating thresholds; (5) placing orders without checking existing position state, potentially re-entering a long position that is already open. The buy-below-30 / sell-above-70 thresholds are unambiguous. The strategy should hold no position between signals. A correct implementation should use AddEquity('SPY', Resolution.Daily), create RSI with period 14, set a warmup period of at least 14 bars, and use OnData or a scheduled event to check thresholds and manage a single long position.

prompts.leak_audit_notes: This is a classic golden cross / death cross strategy on QQQ using daily bars. The primary LEAN-specific failure modes include: (1) insufficient warmup — the algorithm needs at least 200 bars of history before the 200-day SMA is ready, so models must call SetWarmUp(200) or equivalent; (2) cross detection logic — models may naively compare current values without tracking previous-bar state, missing the 'cross' condition and instead triggering on any day the 50 > 200 (which would prevent re-entry logic from working correctly); (3) order management — models may fail to check if already invested before placing a buy order, causing duplicate orders. The prompt is rated mild_variation because there is a small ambiguity around whether to use SetHoldings vs fixed share count, and whether to use a CrossingIndicator helper or manual previous-value tracking. The 2018 start date means the algorithm will need warmup data from late 2017, which LEAN handles via history requests or SetWarmUp. The strategy should produce exactly one or two round-trip trades over the 2018-2024 window given QQQ's price history.
prompts.original_text: Go long QQQ when the 50-day simple moving average crosses above the 200-day simple moving average. Exit the position when the 50-day SMA crosses back below the 200-day. Daily bars, 2018 through 2024

prompts.leak_audit_notes: This prompt is ambiguous in its crossover logic. 'Buy when SMA(200) crosses below' is unclear — crosses below what? Likely intended to mean price crosses above SMA(200) (golden cross signal) or SMA(50) crosses above SMA(200). Similarly, 'sell when SMA(50) crosses above' is incomplete — crosses above what? The most natural interpretation is a dual-SMA crossover system where a buy signal fires when price crosses above SMA(200) and a sell signal fires when price crosses above SMA(50), or alternatively a golden/death cross between SMA(50) and SMA(200). Models may implement this in multiple meaningfully different ways. LEAN-specific failure modes include: not warming up indicators sufficiently (200 bars needed before first valid signal), using CrossingAbove/CrossingBelow indicator helpers incorrectly, or mishandling the asymmetric SMA periods (50 vs 200). The end_date is specified as 01/01/2022 which maps to 2022-01-01. Curators should verify that the chosen crossover interpretation is consistent and that warmup period covers at least 200 trading days.

prompts.leak_audit_notes: This prompt tests multi-asset intraday mean-reversion logic using RSI and MACD on SPY and QQQ at minute resolution. Key LEAN failure modes include: (1) incorrect crossover detection — RSI 'crosses below 30' requires tracking the previous RSI value to detect the transition, not just checking if RSI < 30; (2) MACD 'crosses up' is ambiguous — it could mean MACD line crosses above signal line, MACD histogram crosses zero, or MACD line crosses above zero; (3) indicator warmup period must be handled correctly at minute resolution (MACD default 12/26/9 requires at least 35 bars, RSI default 14 requires 14 bars); (4) the strategy must apply independently to both SPY and QQQ, requiring per-symbol indicator instances; (5) the narrow one-month window (March 2023) means warmup bars must be accounted for — the algorithm should set WarmUpPeriod or use SetWarmUp() to avoid trading on incomplete indicators; (6) position sizing is unspecified, leaving room for variation; (7) the sell condition (MACD crosses up) is independent of the buy condition, which may result in selling before a position is opened if not guarded.

prompts.leak_audit_notes: This prompt tests a basic RSI crossover mean-reversion strategy on SPY at daily resolution. Key LEAN-specific failure modes include: (1) incorrect use of RSI crossover detection — models may check RSI value thresholds each bar rather than using proper CrossBelow/CrossAbove logic or tracking previous RSI values to detect the crossing event; (2) forgetting to warm up the RSI indicator before trading begins, which could cause premature signals; (3) confusion between RSI period (default 14) which is unspecified in the prompt — mild variation is acceptable here; (4) not handling the case where a buy signal fires while already holding a position, or a sell signal fires with no position. The sell condition (RSI > 70) implies an overbought exit, consistent with mean-reversion logic. The date range is explicitly 2020-01-01 to 2022-01-01, which must be respected. Models should use self.rsi.IsReady checks before acting on signals.

prompts.leak_audit_notes: This prompt is intentionally ambiguous about what 'crossed' means for each SMA. The most natural interpretation is a dual-SMA crossover system (price crosses above SMA30 to buy, price crosses below SMA60 to sell), but another valid reading is a golden/death cross between SMA30 and SMA60 themselves. Additionally, the prompt does not specify whether 'crossed' means a price crossover or a moving average crossover against each other. Models may also fail to handle LEAN warmup correctly — SMA(60) requires at least 60 bars of history before it is ready, and failing to set a proper WarmUpPeriod or History call will result in trades firing prematurely. The prompt also does not specify resolution (daily assumed), position sizing (full portfolio assumed), or whether to go long-only or allow short positions. The end date '01/01/2021' is exclusive in LEAN's SetEndDate, so the backtest effectively covers all of 2020. Models should use self.sma30 = self.SMA('TSLA', 30) and self.sma60 = self.SMA('TSLA', 60) with SetWarmUp(60) or equivalent.
